title: Edge Consumption Affinity & Local Cache Playbook
author: Sofia Park
body:
Overview:

This playbook explains the product intent, design trade-offs, and rollout plan for enabling consumption affinity and local cache behavior for edge and near-edge Redwood deployments. The goal is to improve tail-latency for conversational and short-sequence workloads while reducing per-token compute cost through coordinated local caching and affinity routing. This is a product-facing reference for PMs, solutions engineers, and partner integrators.

Key principles:

1) Latency first for interactive workloads: preserve 95th/99th tail latency SLOs for conversational routes (target 95th < 120ms for short prompts in edge regions).
2) Cost-aware fallthroughs: local cache hits reduce GPU token cost; misses should gracefully route to cost-optimized hosted variants without impacting correctness SLA.
3) Consistency and privacy: cached prefixes must honor tenant isolation and retention policies (KMS-backed encryption for private deployments).
4) Observability and rollbackability: every affinity policy must log decision reasons and expose observability hooks for SLO regressions and cost impact.

Scope and components:

- Consumption Affinity Service (CAS): a lightweight control-plane microservice that computes a per-tenant affinity score for edge vs. central serving, based on recent traffic patterns, per-route SLOs, and capacity signals.
- Local Prefetch Proxy (LPP): an optional customer-side (or VPC) proxy that maintains a local prefix/KV cache and prefetches hot model context (embedding vectors and KV segments) from upstream replicas.
- Affinity Router: runtime policy embedded in the gateway which consults CAS to decide request routing: local -> dedicated edge pool -> hosted fallback.
- Cache Coordination Protocol: a compact protocol (HTTP/2+ gRPC) for cache eviction hints, prefetch requests, and lease-based ownership of cached segments.

SLOs and thresholds (product defaults):

- Interactive conversational (short prompts, <256 tokens): 95th latency target = 120ms, 99th = 300ms.
- Cache hit target: 60% steady-state for routes with affinity enabled within first 72 hours after warmup.
- Cost impact guardrail: no single-tenant affinity policy may increase monthly token-related spend by >5% without explicit approval.

Customer-facing behaviors and configs:

Table: default per-route config (text table)

Name | Default | Description
-----|---------|---------
affinity_enabled | true | Whether CAS can set affinity for this route
prefetch_window | 90s | Lookback window for prefetch heuristics
min_traffic_for_affinity | 100 req/day | Minimum traffic to qualify for persistent affinity
cache_ttl | 6h | Default lease/TLL for prefetched KV segments
fallback_model_tier | standard | Model tier used when local misses occur

How affinity decisions work (high level):

1. Route registers with CAS with route metadata (SLO, expected seq length distribution, tenant id).
2. CAS ingests traffic telemetry (per-route QPS, recent cache hit rate, tail latency) and computes an affinity score (0.0-1.0) based on configured weights: latency_weight (0.5), hit_rate_weight (0.3), cost_delta_weight (0.2).
3. If score > 0.7 and capacity is available in edge pool, CAS marks route as Affinity=LOCAL and issues prefetch hints to LPP.
4. Affinity Router enforces a small percentage of canary bypasses (2%) to validate quality against hosted baseline.

Operational runbook (for product and SRE):

Pre-deployment checklist:
- Confirm tenant encryption keys available (KMS).
- Verify edge pool capacity >= expected steady-state QPS for routes marked local.
- Enable affinity in staging and validate hit-rate >= 40% after warmup.

Incident handling (high level):
1. Symptom: sudden drop in cache hit-rate or spike in tail latency in an edge region.
2. Page oncall SRE and tag the route in CAS UI.
3. Actions: (a) revert route affinity to FALLBACK for affected tenants; (b) invalidate suspicious LPP caches by issuing eviction hints; (c) collect KV cache diagnostic bundle from LPP (see diagnostics API).
4. Postmortem: update prefetch heuristics or raise min_traffic_for_affinity if instability is workload-driven.

Rollout plan (Q4 2026 -> Q1 2027):

- Phase 0 (pilot): select 3 enterprise customers with strict latency needs and low privacy constraints. Deploy LPP and enable Affinity in a single edge region. Collect metrics for 4 weeks.
- Phase 1 (early access): open to more customers with an opt-in flag in Console; expose per-route configuration controls and cost-impact simulator.
- Phase 2 (general availability): enable automatic affinity suggestions for qualifying routes and add self-serve toggle in Console with default safe thresholds.

Pricing and packaging implications:

- Affinity-enabled routes will qualify for a reduced token charge on local cache hits (example: 40% discount on per-token compute metric for hits), implemented as a post-processing credit applied to invoices.
- Dedicated edge pools used for affinity will be eligible for reserved-capacity pricing; product must surface guidance on commit sizing (recommended 30% headroom).
- Premium support add-on: affinity stabilization SLA (four-week warmup assistance and weekly health check-ins).

Console and API examples:

- Sample API: enable affinity on route via Redwood API (curl)

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/route-123/affinity \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"affinity_enabled": true, "min_traffic_for_affinity": 200, "cache_ttl_seconds": 14400}'

- Affinity decision query (gRPC snippet concept):
// affinity_service.getAffinity(route_id, tenant_id) -> {score: 0.82, reason: ["low_tail_latency", "high_local_hit_rate"]}

Monitoring and telemetry requirements:

- Telemetry events to emit: affinity_evaluation, cache_prefetch_hint, cache_hit, cache_miss, affinity_enforcement_event.
- Dashboards: per-region affinity hit-rate, per-route tail-latency vs. baseline, monthly cost delta for affinity-enabled tenants.
- Alerts: cache_hit_rate < 40% sustained for 30m, or tail_latency_95th increase > 30% vs baseline.

Security and compliance notes:

- All cache contents must be encrypted at rest using customer KMS keys for Private deployments.
- Prefetch requests must carry tenant scoping headers and be rate-limited (default 10 prefetches/sec per tenant).
- For regulated customers, affinity can be restricted to dedicated private edge pools only.

Decision log (why we chose this approach):

- Alternatives considered: purely central caching, full-model replication to every edge, and client-side only caching.
- Tradeoffs: model replication provides best latency but unacceptable cost and variant proliferation; client-only caching lacks coordination and instrumentation. Consumption Affinity + coordinated prefetch gives a practical middle ground with measurable cost and latency improvements.

Open questions and follow-ups:

- Quantify warmup curve behavior across multi-tenant noisy neighbors and update prefetch heuristics accordingly.
- Define SLO for prefetch bandwidth costs and establish billing for heavy prefetch consumers.
- Evaluate stronger consistency modes (read-through vs. lease-based) for high-security customers.

Appendix: example prefetch heuristics pseudocode

// simplified scoring for whether to prefetch a prefix
function should_prefetch(route_metrics) {
  score = 0
  if (route_metrics.qps > 5) score += 0.4
  if (route_metrics.recent_cache_hits > 0.5) score += 0.3
  if (route_metrics.tail_latency > baseline * 1.2) score += 0.3
  return score > 0.6
}

Diagnostic CLI (LPP) to collect cache bundle:

redwood-lpp collect-cache-bundle --route route-123 --output /tmp/route-123-cache-bundle.tgz
